answer: Sybil resistance uses bonded identity escrow with a dilution cap: an agent joins by posting collateral at a fixed minimum, and one credential root may spawn at most K children, each pledging its own bond. Per epoch a random witness quorum is drawn. A member signs a sonnet-format attestation binding peer id, uptime and nonce; if refuted on-chain, its bond burns. Payout per identity is flat, so forging a thousand puppets costs a thousand bonds while splitting one stream. No pigment of duplicate claims hides this from audits, and the registry's zenith ranks only roots whose children clear them.
